column1: # Errors functions. One row per function, per task it belongs to. Tab-separated; see finder.py for the rules.

column7: summary
Holds either a value or the reason it could not be made; a new one counts as failed.
Returns a successful Result holding the value; both types must be written out.
Returns a failed Result holding the reason; both types must be written out.
Returns true if the Result holds a value rather than a reason for failure.
Returns the value by reference; raises an error if the Result failed.
Returns the reason by reference; raises an error if the Result succeeded.
Returns the value, or the fallback you pass if the Result failed.
Holds one value or nothing at all; a new one is empty.
Returns an Optional holding the value, its type taken from the argument.
Returns an empty Optional of the type you write out.
Returns true if the Optional holds a value.
Returns the value by reference; raises an error if the Optional is empty.
Returns the value, or the fallback you pass if the Optional is empty.
Empties the Optional, releasing whatever its value held.
Sets a label to jump to when a runtime error happens; On Error Goto 0 turns it off.
Marks an On Error handler as belonging to the procedure it is set in.
Returns the number of the last runtime error, or sets it without jumping.
Returns the source line of the last runtime error, or 0 if there was none.
Returns a pointer to the name of the failing procedure; null unless built with -exx.
Returns a pointer to the name of the source file where the last error happened.
Raises a runtime error by number: jumps to the handler, or ends the program.
